rules.title: AB 325: Ban on using or distributing a common pricing algorithm as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade
rules.requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce under the Cartwright Act. A common pricing algorithm is any methodology or technology used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or influence a price or commercial term, which can include rents.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person, as defined in Bus. & Prof. Code § 16702, who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm. This includes selling, licensing, or providing access to one. End consumers are excluded. The law is general antitrust law, not limited to rental housing.
rules.exemptions: End consumers of a product or service are not 'persons' under the section.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires use of a common pricing algorithm used by two or more persons that uses competitor data, as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade.

rules.penalty: Cartwright Act enforcement, under which violations are punishable as a crime. A complaint need only plausibly allege a contract, combination, or conspiracy and need not allege facts excluding independent action (Bus. & Prof. Code § 16756.1).
rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(a) (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.conflict_note: The document shows only the chaptered date (approved Oct 6, 2025) and no urgency clause. The effective date of Jan 1, 2026 is inferred from California's default rule for regular-session statutes. This is a general antitrust provision that applies to rental pricing algorithms but is not specific to housing.

rules.title: AB 325: Ban on coercing adoption of prices or terms recommended by a common pricing algorithm
rules.requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm while coercing another person to set or adopt a price or commercial term recommended by the algorithm for the same or similar products or services in California. Commercial terms include level of service, availability, and output.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person, as defined in Bus. & Prof. Code § 16702, who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm and coerces another person to adopt its recommended price or term. End consumers are excluded. The law is general antitrust law, not limited to rental housing.
rules.exemptions: End consumers of a product or service are not 'persons' under the section.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires coercion of another person to adopt a price or commercial term recommended by a common pricing algorithm.

rules.penalty: Cartwright Act enforcement, under which violations are punishable as a crime.
rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(b) (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
rules.quoted_span: (b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.
rules.conflict_note: The document shows only the chaptered date (approved Oct 6, 2025) and no urgency clause. The effective date of Jan 1, 2026 is inferred from California's default rule for regular-session statutes. This is a general antitrust provision that applies to rental pricing algorithms but is not specific to housing.
